headline: Zheng-Dao's 'Heaven's Ledger' Platform Enters Orbit — Rivals Sound Alarm
body:
Zheng-Dao Corporation successfully deployed its Heaven's Ledger orbital platform at 14:37 UTC on Sunday, completing a launch sequence from their Geartown vertical launch facility that had been under construction since 2168. The platform, described by Zheng-Dao's Chief Orbital Officer Wen Larocque-Adeyemi as 'a sovereign commercial node above all jurisdictions,' carries communications relay arrays, quantum data vaults, and — according to intelligence assessments shared with the Lake Monitor — weapons-grade surveillance optics capable of resolving individual BCI signatures from low orbit. Zheng-Dao has declined to address the surveillance claims.

The launch has drawn sharp responses from competitor corponations, with Axiom filing an emergency protest with the Quanta Arbitration Framework and Sterling-Nakamura issuing a joint statement with Palladian calling Heaven's Ledger 'a unilateral escalation of the sovereignty arms race.' Arcturus Defense, notably, issued no statement — prompting widespread speculation that the two corponations have a classified partnership arrangement. 'If Zheng-Dao can read your BCI handshake from orbit,' noted Graycloaks analyst Kofi Steele-Vasquez in a public brief, 'every encrypted deal in GLMZ just got a little less encrypted.'

The Federal Remnant's Space Commerce Division acknowledged the launch but confirmed it lacks any legal mechanism to compel inspection or regulate the platform's systems. On the streets of The Circuit, reactions ranged from awe to alarm. 'I watched it pass last night,' said Mireille Tanaka-Obi, a systems trader operating out of Circuit Row 9. 'Bright as a star and owned by a corp. That should terrify everyone.'
aftermath: Within 90 days of launch, three separate corponations — Tessera, Ringo, and Sterling-Nakamura — had begun accelerated orbital program funding, igniting what analysts would later call the Meridian Space Race.
runner_relevance: Heaven's Ledger's launch created a wave of high-stakes runner contracts almost immediately: competing corponations hired data-retrieval specialists to acquire Zheng-Dao's orbital technical schematics, and protection contracts surged for Zheng-Dao engineers who suddenly became extraction targets. The platform's surveillance capability made runners with ECM (electronic countermeasure) expertise suddenly premium commodities, as clients paying for sensitive operations needed BCI-masking during open-air work. Graycloaks began brokering information about Heaven's Ledger's orbital windows — when the platform was overhead vs. blind — selling that data to anyone running contracts that required avoiding surveillance.
